| 🪢 Tangle · [q-0037.0013.0006](docs/questions/q-0037.0013.0006-how-is-the-path-ahead-found-and-shown-the-space-of-open-questions-and-tickets-mapped-from-the-roots-the-next-slices-ranked-by-a-stated-criterion-and-the-picture.md) · [q-0037.0012.0009](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0009-how-is-an-amendment-to-an-instruction-tested-before-it-lands-against-which-cases-chosen-how-run-with-no-instruction-the-standing-one-and-the-new-one.md) · — · — |
|---|

| 📍 **q-0037.0013.0006** · How is the path ahead found and shown: the space of open questions and tickets mapped from the roots, the next slices ranked by a stated criterion, and the picture the person sees? |
|---|

**The driver, plainly.** Today the ring is run by one agent: it reads the skills in turn, judges its own plan, judges its own verification, decides itself when to go back, and you read the result afterwards. The driver is the script that runs that sequence for a chosen ticket instead. Given the ticket, it calls `/plan`; hands the RFC to a judge agent that has none of the writer's context and asks whether it stands against the governing docs; loops until the judge passes or the count runs out; calls `/implement`; runs the verification set; hands the criteria that need judgment to a judge; and on a finding decides repeat, return upstream, or stop at the dial for you. It is what the doc-rule bench did by hand for one rule change, writer, judge and runner, made standing and applied to every ticket. It is your own sentence from two turns ago, *something mechanical that owns the judges and the reiterations*, and I gave it a name because the pacer's name had come to mean three things.

**The split, in those terms.** The pacer promised three answers: which work comes next; which step comes next inside that work and how the steps are run; and where a session resumes. The pathfinder is the first. The driver, with the ring's rules it executes, is the second. The third already exists, the store's position and the ticket's status, which `/recall` reads today. Nothing is left for the word *pacer* to name. That is the whole of the split.

**On *build nothing*: you are right, and I registered it.** Twice I read Occam as *do nothing* when the work had met a better abstraction whose cases stand in five places unlinked. Five unlinked expressions are more parts than one named principle that five rules cite, so Occam itself says to name it. The rule that should have fired speaks only of a reply's citations, not of a principle met in the work, so the slip is rule failure 54, with its amendment proposed there (💡 [*Self-improvement*](AGENTS.md:174)):

🧩 **Proposed rule — [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) · General rules, *Occam***

> A principle the work meets expressed in several places is named once at a home and cited from each; that is fewer parts, not more.

And the realignment the backtrack asks for, as I see it. The principle gets a home in the method's glossary, and the five rules that are its cases cite it, their wording improved where the name makes a sentence shorter:

✏️ **Proposed change — [.agents/glossary.md](.agents/glossary.md) · new term**

> **Backtrack**: The return from a method to the abstraction it was derived from, when deriving shows the abstraction missing, wrong or incomplete. Its moves are the store's: open the missing parent, reword, re-parent, bind a straw dog to what will change; and the step's: return upstream. The pathfinder redraws the path after each.

The five citing places: the shape's structure rule in the entry file; the straw dog section; the missing-parent clause of Q1; the reword call in the questions skill; and the step-end rule, where *return upstream* finally lands from the pacer page. Both texts are 🛠️ self-improvement=a rule, at the dial, so they are shown here and land on your yes (💡 [*At the dial it settles, and shows the person before acting*](AGENTS.md:220)). The q-0037.0001.0023 half, how a change in one answer reaches what stood on it, stays open; naming the backtrack does not answer it.

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| The amendment to *Occam*, rule failure 54's |
| *Backtrack* as a glossary term, cited from its five places, *return upstream* landed with it |
| The split: pathfinder, driver, the ring's rules; the pacer's name retired |
| Reword and move this question out from under the pacer, and open the driver's beside it |
| Commit the question's body and the register entry as they stand |
| [q-0037.0012.0003](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0003-what-does-an-entry-contract-version-cover.md) waits at `/align`, as the queue has held since 2026-10-08 |
